commentary_title: Aframax demand eases but smaller CPC cargoes spark more enquiry
commentary_summary: The Aframax tonne-miles index slipped to 94.6 in week 46 accompanied by lower utilisation compared with the previous week signalling softer overall demand for the segment. | Both ballast and laden speeds stayed broadly stable while the share of laden tonnage declined, more notably in the East and slightly in the West. | Some CPC cargoes that are usually big enough for Suezmax ships are now being reduced in size, so they can be loaded on Aframax ships instead. Thus, charterers are starting to look for more Aframax vessels which could increase Aframax demand soon.
